newsitem.title: INDIA: India's Congress group asks Rao to resign as chief.
newsitem.headline: India's Congress group asks Rao to resign as chief.

text.p: Senior colleagues of former Indian prime minister P.V. Narasimha Rao called on him to resign on Wednesday from his last official post in the Congress Party.

Rao, who led Congress to its worst defeat ever in general elections earlier this year, resigned as party president in September after a court summoned him to testify in court in a criminal conspiracy case. He denied any wrongdoing in the case.

All 24 members of the executive committee of the party's parliamentary bloc asked Rao, who faces charges in three separate corruption cases, to quit but Rao said he would only consider the formal request to stand down.

"We the elected members of the executive committee of the Congress Parliamentary Party (CPP) ...feel the need of change in the leadership of the CPP and request the leader to step down," the committee's members said in a letter.
"I will consider the letter," Rao was quoted as saying by a CPP member, Praful Patel at a meeting of the executive committee on Wednesday.
Patel said the letter was read out by Priya Ranjan Das Munsi, one of Rao's biggest critics.
Rao has retained clout as head of the parliamentary delegation that offers make-or-break support to Prime Minister H.D. Deve Gowda's 13-party coalition that won power in June.
Recently, party leaders, following a shake-up within the CPP, stepped up demands for Rao to quit as the CPP's chief.

Wednesday's letter marked a final assault on Rao to resign from the post as head of the group that has a total strength of 229 legislators, 140 of whom are from the 545-member lower house, Lok Sabha. The rest are in the upper house, Rajya Sabha.
The letter was intended to be a resolution to be moved at the committee's meeting, but Rao refused to accept it, saying notice had not been given under party rules, CPP members said.
"Then you accept it (the letter) as our feeling," Patel quoted Das Munsi as saying at the meeting.
The move to oust Rao was widely seen to be supported by Sitaram Kesri, who succeeded Rao as party chief in September.
Rao, charged in three corruption cases. has denied any wrongdoing. But his party's image is widely seen as having suffered because of the cases.
CPP members praised Rao's leadership since 1991, when he took over the party after the murder of former prime minister Rajiv Gandhi, but said that the party needed to be strengthened.
"In this context it has become absolutely necessary to establish credibility of the party in the eyes of the people as this has suffered much due to recent happenings," they said.
